documents.title: H&P - Admission - Community-Acquired Pneumonia
lines: ADMISSION H&P
HD1 Time of eval: 21:40
CHIEF COMPLAINT: cough, fever, new confusion
HPI:
59 yo male brought in by son for 6 days of productive cough, fevers to 39.1 at home, and progressive dyspnea.
Cough initially dry, now productive of rust-colored sputum. Pleuritic right-sided chest pain with deep breath.
New [confusion] per son, who reports patient is normally independent - works full time, drives, manages own meds.
Son states pt was confusing the bathroom door for the front door this morning and repeating questions.
On arrival pt oriented to self only; could not state month or location.
[prior antibiotic]: urgent care prescribed doxycycline 4 days ago; took all doses; fever and cough worsened.
No vomiting. Poor oral intake for 2 days, mostly sips of water. No diarrhea.
No recent travel, no sick contacts, no aspiration event witnessed. No hemoptysis beyond sputum tinge.
ROS: denies headache, no neck stiffness, no rash, no dysuria, no leg swelling. Otherwise per HPI.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Type 2 diabetes, HbA1c 7.4 three months ago per outside records
Hypertension
Former smoker, 20 pack-years, quit 6 years ago
Remote left inguinal hernia repair
HOME MEDICATIONS:
metformin 1000 mg PO BID
lisinopril 20 mg PO daily
atorvastatin 20 mg PO daily
ALLERGIES: no known drug allergies
SOCIAL: lives alone in apartment; son lives 10 min away and checks in. No alcohol excess, no drug use.
FAMILY HISTORY: father MI age 70, mother DM2
TRIAGE VITALS:
T 38.9 C, HR 108, BP 132/78, [respiratory rate] 32 at triage, 30 at 4 hours
[SpO2] 93% on RA at triage
PHYSICAL EXAM:
Gen: ill-appearing, mildly diaphoretic, speaking in short phrases
Neuro: awake, oriented to self only, follows simple commands, no focal deficit, no asterixis
HEENT: dry mucous membranes, no meningismus
Resp: tachypneic, accessory muscle use, crackles right base and right axilla, dullness to percussion right base
CV: tachycardic, regular, no murmur, JVP not elevated
Abd: soft, nontender, no organomegaly
Ext: no edema, warm, cap refill brisk
Skin: no rash
LABS ON ARRIVAL:
WBC 17.6 with 88% neutrophils, bands 9%
Hgb 13.8, plt 231
[BUN] 34 mg/dL, sodium 127 mEq/L on arrival
Creatinine 1.24, K 4.1, HCO3 22, glucose 188
Lactate 1.9, procalcitonin 3.8
LFTs within normal limits
Blood cultures x2 drawn prior to antibiotics; sputum Gram stain and culture sent; resp viral panel and pneumococcal urinary antigen sent
IMAGING:
Chest x-ray: right lower and right middle lobe [infiltrate] with small right pleural effusion.
Effusion too small to tap safely at bedside per ED read.
ASSESSMENT:
59 yo male with severe community-acquired pneumonia involving RML and RLL, small parapneumonic effusion, hyponatremia and azotemia, and acute encephalopathy.
[CURB-65] of 3 (confusion, BUN >19 mg/dL, RR >=30). Admit to stepdown telemetry.
Failed outpatient doxycycline argues for broader coverage and inpatient management.
PLAN:
[ceftriaxone] 1 g IV once in the ED, then continue ceftriaxone 1 g IV q24h plus azithromycin 500 mg IV daily
Titrate O2 to keep SpO2 >=92%; incentive spirometry q1h while awake
Repeat Na and BUN in AM; encourage PO intake, no free water restriction for now
Hold metformin and lisinopril while acutely ill
Acetaminophen 650 mg PO q6h prn fever; sliding scale insulin q6h
Delirium precautions: lights on during day, glasses at bedside, minimize night checks, family at bedside
Follow blood cultures; call with any new O2 requirement above 4L NC or worsening work of breathing

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 AM
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD2 07:20
SUBJECTIVE:
Pt slept in intervals. RN notes [SpO2] 91% while sleeping at 02:10, 1L NC placed overnight with improvement to 95%.
This AM pt oriented to self, place, and year with prompting - marked improvement per son at bedside.
Cough remains productive, less pleuritic pain. Ate 60% of breakfast without difficulty swallowing.
O2: 1L NC, currently SpO2 96%.
EXAM:
Gen: more interactive, sitting up in chair
Resp: crackles right base persist, decreased breath sounds right base, no accessory muscle use at rest
CV: regular, no murmur
Neuro: attention improved, follows multistep commands
LABS:
WBC 14.2 (from 17.6), Na 130, BUN 28, Cr 1.06, glucose 154
Blood cultures x2 no growth at 12h; resp viral panel negative; pneumococcal urinary antigen positive
Sputum culture pending, Gram stain with gram-positive diplococci
ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
1. Severe CAP, RML/RLL with small right effusion - clinically improving. Afebrile trend, WBC down.
Tolerating oral diet and switched to oral cefpodoxime 200 mg PO BID this morning; continue azithromycin 500 mg PO daily.
Effusion small and pt improving - no thoracentesis at this time, will repeat imaging if fever or hypoxemia recurs.
2. Hypoxemia - wean O2 as tolerated, target SpO2 >=92%. Ambulate with pulse ox today.
3. Encephalopathy - resolving with treatment of infection. Continue delirium precautions, no sedatives.
4. Hyponatremia/azotemia - improving with PO intake. Recheck BMP in AM.
5. DM2 - metformin still held, sliding scale insulin, fingersticks q6h.
6. Incentive spirometry q1h while awake, up in chair for all meals.
Discussed plan with son; likely 1-2 more days inpatient.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD3
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD3 08:05
SUBJECTIVE:
Pt reports best night so far, slept 6h uninterrupted. No dyspnea at rest, cough less frequent and looser.
Oriented x4 this morning, recalls admission events, asking about going home.
Ambulated hallway x2 yesterday evening with RN, no desaturation below 93%.
VITALS (24h): Tmax 37.6, afebrile since 20:00. HR 78-88. BP 126/76. RR 18-20.
O2: weaned off NC at 22:30 last night, SpO2 94-96% on RA including with ambulation.
EXAM:
Gen: comfortable, no distress, eating breakfast
Resp: scattered right basilar crackles, improved air movement, no dullness noted today over lower zones
CV: regular rate, no murmur, no edema
Abd: soft, nontender
Neuro: alert, oriented x4, attention intact, normal gait with standby assist
LABS:
WBC 9.8, Hgb 13.2, plt 278
Na 134, K 4.0, BUN 19, Cr 0.94, glucose 142
Blood cultures x2 no growth at 36h
Sputum culture: S. pneumoniae, pan-sensitive including to beta-lactams
ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
1. Pneumococcal CAP, RML/RLL with small right effusion - much improved on day 3.
Continue cefpodoxime 200 mg PO BID; azithromycin PO daily, plan total 5-7 day course.
No repeat CXR needed now given clinical improvement; outpatient imaging in 6-8 weeks given smoking history.
2. Resolved hypoxemia - off O2 >8h, maintain on RA.
3. Resolved encephalopathy - back to baseline per son.
4. Hyponatremia/azotemia - nearly corrected with PO intake.
5. DM2 - resume metformin tomorrow if Cr stable; restart lisinopril at discharge.
6. Anticipate discharge HD4 if remains afebrile on RA overnight. PT screen not required, ambulating independently.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Community-Acquired Pneumonia
lines: DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit HD1, discharge HD4 at 11:30. Length of stay 4 days.
DISCHARGE DIAGNOSIS: Community-acquired pneumonia, S. pneumoniae, right middle and right lower lobe, with small right pleural effusion
SECONDARY: acute encephalopathy (resolved), hypoxemia (resolved), hyponatremia (resolved), T2DM, HTN
BRIEF HOSPITAL COURSE:
59 yo male presented with 6 days of fever and productive cough after failing outpatient therapy.
[prior antibiotic]: urgent care prescribed doxycycline 4 days ago; took all doses; fever and cough worsened.
[confusion] was new per son, who reports patient is normally independent; oriented to self only on arrival.
Triage vitals notable for [respiratory rate] 32 at triage, 30 at 4 hours, and [SpO2] 93% on RA at triage.
Labs on arrival: WBC 17.6, [BUN] 34 mg/dL, sodium 127 mEq/L on arrival, Cr 1.24, lactate 1.9.
Chest x-ray: right lower and right middle lobe [infiltrate] with small right pleural effusion.
[CURB-65] of 3 documented in the admitting note; admitted to stepdown telemetry.
[ceftriaxone] 1 g IV once in the ED, then ceftriaxone q24h with azithromycin.
1L NC placed overnight for SpO2 91% while sleeping, weaned off O2 on HD3 at 22:30 the prior night.
Tolerating oral diet and switched to oral cefpodoxime the next morning after admission; azithromycin converted to PO same day.
Sputum culture grew pan-sensitive S. pneumoniae; pneumococcal urinary antigen positive; blood cultures x2 no growth at 72h; resp viral panel negative.
Effusion remained small and pt improved clinically - no drainage required.
Mental status returned to baseline by HD3, oriented x4 and ambulating independently.
DISCHARGE VITALS: T 36.9, HR 76, BP 124/78, RR 18, SpO2 96% on RA, ambulatory sat 94%.
DISCHARGE LABS: WBC 7.9, Na 137, BUN 15, Cr 0.92, glucose 138.
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
cefpodoxime 200 mg PO BID to complete 3 more days
azithromycin 500 mg PO daily to complete 1 more day
resume metformin 1000 mg PO BID
resume lisinopril 20 mg PO daily
resume atorvastatin 20 mg PO daily
acetaminophen 650 mg PO q6h prn
FOLLOW UP:
Primary care in 5-7 days for symptom check and repeat BMP.
Outpatient chest x-ray in 6-8 weeks given 20 pack-year smoking history; discuss lung cancer screening.
Pneumococcal and influenza vaccination at follow up visit.
INSTRUCTIONS: finish all antibiotics, incentive spirometry 10x hourly while awake, increase fluids, daily walks.
Return for fever above 38.3, new confusion, worsening shortness of breath, or chest pain.
Discharge teaching completed with pt and son at bedside; both verbalized understanding.
Pt left unit ambulatory with son.
